_note: Every human-facing sentence on the site lives here so it can be rewritten. Text in {braces} is filled in by scripts/build_site.py from data/summary.json or from the data files; never type a number here.

nav.search_empty: No matching results, papers or Lean statements.

words.main_result: In OpenAI’s list of main results
words.supporting_result: Outside OpenAI’s list of main results

home.title: OpenAI Math Atlas
home.lede: An independent guide to OpenAI’s mathematics release: {manuscripts} manuscripts in {families} families of related papers, grouped into {disciplines} disciplines. The release links {lean} Comparator challenge files to {families_with_lean} families, and each family page quotes OpenAI’s notes on their scope.
home.map_help: Choose a discipline, then a family. Press Escape or select empty map space to go back; the browser’s Back button retraces your steps.
home.area_note: Each family’s area reflects its manuscript count.
home.search_label: Find a family by title, number or challenge name
home.search_placeholder: Find a family by title, number or challenge
home.search_more: Showing {shown} of {total} matches. The list beside the map shows them all.
home.map_failed: The map could not load. Every family is listed by discipline below.
home.list_none: No family in this view matches the search.
home.legend_lean_main: A Comparator statement OpenAI lists as a main result
home.legend_lean_support: Comparator statements, none in OpenAI’s list of main results
home.legend_size_note: The largest count of local vocabulary declarations among a family’s challenge files: definitions, types, instances, notation, macros and axioms detected in the file. Theorem and lemma declarations are excluded. The count describes the file; it measures neither difficulty nor correctness.
home.legend_citations_0: Cited by no manuscript in another family
home.legend_citations_1: Cited by one manuscript in another family
home.legend_citations_note: These links come from the manuscripts’ bibliographies. Choose a family to draw what it cites and what cites it; lines are drawn only inside the open view, and the card lists every link across the release.
home.legend_explained_none: No explanation recorded in the atlas yet
home.legend_explained_note: A recorded explanation can cover one lemma or the whole result; its page states its scope.
home.caption_idle: {families} families in {disciplines} disciplines. Choose a discipline to open it.
home.caption_discipline: {name}: {families} families, {manuscripts} manuscripts. Choose a family for its card.
home.card_no_lean: No Comparator statement is linked to this family in the release.
home.card_cited_by: Families whose manuscripts cite this one
home.card_vocab_pure: Imports only Mathlib; no local vocabulary added
home.card_scope: Scope, by a draft AI reading of OpenAI’s note: {label}
home.card_scope_stale: Scope reading withheld: it was made for a different version of the release
home.card_mixed: This family’s statements differ in scope, or are not all classified; the colour shows the strongest classified statement.
home.card_explained_none: The atlas has no explanation recorded for this family yet.
home.card_explained_progress: An explanation is in progress; the family page links the draft.
home.card_explained_done: A reviewed explanation is recorded; its page states what it covers.
home.no_js: The map needs JavaScript. Every family is listed by discipline below.
home.numbers_intro: Each number is counted from the release at the pinned commit. Follow a number to its exact definition and counting rule.
home.credit_within_text: The manuscripts in the collection that other manuscripts cite most, from their bibliographies, with whether each has an accompanying Comparator statement.
home.credit_outside_text: The manuscripts cite {works} automatically grouped references outside the release. {top1} and {top2} are cited by the most manuscripts.
home.index_heading: The catalogue: every family, by discipline
home.index_intro: The same {families} families as the map, as a list of full titles.
home.card_cited_count: Cited by {n} manuscripts in other families
home.card_cited_count_one: Cited by 1 manuscript in another family
home.where_label: Where you are in the map
home.legend_covers_source: Scope according to OpenAI’s notes, in a draft reading by an AI agent that no person has reviewed. Each tile shows the strongest classified statement in its family.
home.legend_covers_part: States part of the headline theorem
home.legend_covers_less: States a consequence or a weaker form
home.legend_covers_mixed: Corner mark: statements differ in scope or are not all classified
home.legend_covers_stale: The draft scope reading was made for a different version of the release, so no scope colours are shown.
home.legend_covers_note: Each statement page quotes OpenAI’s note beside the draft reading. Corrections are welcome.
home.legend_community_2: Two or more linked pieces of public work
home.legend_community_1: One linked piece of public work
home.legend_community_note: Replays, error reports, follow-up results, explanations and commentary by other people, each credited and linked on the family’s page.
home.credit_community_text: OpenAI’s repository, the atlas’s own checks, and other people’s public work, each credited at the point where it is used.
home.legend_type_none: No label in the Tier List
home.legend_type_note: As the OpenAI Math Tier List classifies each result. The atlas has not checked every label; corrections are welcome.
home.legend_tier_1: Tiers 0 and 1: landmark or Fields Medal level, if correct
home.legend_tier_4: Tiers 4 to 7: specialist journal to thesis
home.legend_tier_none: No tier in the Tier List
home.legend_tier_note: One public ranking’s judgement of how significant each result would be if it holds up (the OpenAI Math Tier List). It assumes each claim is correct; nothing in it is verified.

family.description_more: Read the rest of OpenAI’s description
family.headline_note: Statements selected automatically from the TeX sources because they appear before the paper’s second section or are marked as main results. Each excerpt links to its source.
family.no_headline: The atlas found no headline statement in this manuscript’s TeX source.
family.lean_scope_heading: OpenAI’s note on what the Lean statements cover
family.readings_intro: People outside OpenAI have read this family's challenge statements against its headline. Their verdicts, in their own terms and credited, sit beside OpenAI's note. Where they differ, both stand.
family.lean_scope_source: From the release’s Lean notes for this result
family.no_lean: No Comparator statement is linked to this family in the release.
family.citations_intro: These links come from the manuscripts’ bibliographies. A citation records that one manuscript cites another; how each cited result is used has not been examined here.
family.cites_intro: Manuscripts in the collection that this family’s manuscripts cite.
family.cites_none: Its manuscripts cite no other manuscript in the collection.
family.cited_intro: Manuscripts in the collection that cite this family’s manuscripts.
family.cited_none: No other manuscript in the collection cites it.
family.refs_intro: Outside works the manuscripts cite, with where in each manuscript the citation appears.
family.refs_none: The atlas found no outside references in this manuscript’s sources.
family.superseded: This is an earlier edition. The current edition is {link}.
family.explain_none: The atlas has no explanation recorded for this family yet. The papers and OpenAI’s notes are below.
family.explain_progress_intro: Drafts recorded in the atlas’s repository. No reviewer has approved them yet.
family.check_choose: Check a statement: choose one of {n}
family.check_choose_intro: Each statement is checked on its own. Choose the one you have read:
family.contribute_intro: Each link opens a GitHub form with this page and the pinned commit filled in. Opening a form reserves nothing.
family.xref_title: A cross-reference to {label} in the paper
family.method_notes: OpenAI’s method notes for this result
family.reasoning_summary: OpenAI released an abridged summary of the model's reasoning for this result:
family.formulations_intro: Propositions extracted from the project’s Model.lean file, listed for comparison with the paper, with any linked Comparator statement beside them. The list comes from a source scan; inclusion records no build or replay.
family.formulations_more: {n} more formulations are in the same file.
family.formulations_theorems: The source scan also found {n} theorem or lemma declarations whose names contain ‘manuscript’.

explanation.reviewed_note: Recorded in the atlas as reviewed. The reviewer and the scope of the review are listed below.
explanation.version: Release version it was written against
explanation.older_version: An earlier version of the release than this atlas shows.
explanation.description: An explanation of part or all of result {id} in OpenAI’s mathematics release: {title}.

statement.claim_lean_intro: The lines of the challenge file that state the theorem, then the definitions in the file that it uses.
statement.defs_intro: Local definitions the statement names, followed through the definitions they name in turn. The match is by name in the source text, so a name reached only through notation can be missed; the full file is below.
statement.defs_more: {n} more definitions are reached the same way; the full file lists them.
statement.sorry_note: A Comparator challenge file states the theorem and leaves its proof as `sorry` on purpose. OpenAI’s proof is in the solution module listed here, and Comparator is the tool that checks that proof against this statement.
statement.sorry_note_axiom: A Comparator challenge file states the theorem and leaves its proof open. This file writes `axiom mainStatement` where others write `sorry`; OpenAI’s solution module proves `main` directly, and Comparator is the tool that checks that proof against this statement.
statement.main_yes: OpenAI lists this as a main result in its Lean catalogue.
statement.main_no: OpenAI’s Lean catalogue leaves this outside its main results; the release’s Lean notes for result {id} link it.
statement.permitted_axioms_note: The axioms this configuration allows a proof to use. The list is an allowance; which axioms a proof uses is shown by a replay.
statement.lines: Lines of Lean, without comments or blank lines
statement.vocab_heading: Local vocabulary declarations in this file
statement.vocab_intro: The definitions, types, instances, notation, macros and axioms detected in this file. Theorem and lemma declarations are excluded. Reading the theorem also needs its imports and any definitions supplied by the solution library.
statement.vocab_none: This file adds no definitions, types, instances, notation, macros or axioms. Its imports are listed above.
statement.vocab_pure: This file imports only Mathlib and adds no local vocabulary, so its statement is written in Mathlib’s vocabulary.
statement.axiom_heading: A note on how this file states its claim
statement.axiom_note: Line {line} of this statement file writes `axiom mainStatement : MainClaim` where other statement files write `sorry`. It stands in for the proof on the statement side only. OpenAI’s solution proves `main` directly, in {solution_link}. A successful Comparator replay checks the solution against the allowed axioms: {axioms}.
statement.scope_full: OpenAI’s full Lean note for result {id}
statement.scope_source: From the release’s Lean notes for result {id}
statement.paper_heading: Every extracted statement of the accompanying papers
statement.paper_intro: The statements the atlas extracted automatically from each accompanying paper’s TeX source, with links to the full sources.
statement.all_statements_link: Every extracted statement of the papers is listed under supporting material.
statement.file_intro: {lines} lines, exactly as in the release at the pinned commit.
statement.card_intro: A card for sharing, made from the same record as this page. It carries the pairing, scope and review states with it.
statement.card_paper_candidate: Candidate paper statement, chosen automatically by word overlap; not reviewed
statement.card_paper_abstain_weak: The automatic word-overlap match was too weak to pick a paper statement, so none is shown here.
statement.card_paper_abstain_tie: Two paper statements matched equally well by word overlap, so neither is shown here.
statement.card_paper_abstain_none: The atlas found no extracted statement in the accompanying papers.
statement.card_scope: Scope, by a draft AI reading of OpenAI’s note: {label}
statement.card_scope_stale: Scope reading withheld: made for a different version of the release
statement.card_vocab_pure: Imports only Mathlib; no local vocabulary added
statement.card_pairing: The paper statement on the card was chosen automatically by word overlap with the Lean labels, names, docstrings and scope note, and only when the overlap was strong enough. Every extracted statement is listed under supporting material.
statement.card_continues: The statement continues in the paper.
statement.reruns_intro: Other people have run this challenge through Comparator themselves. Each line is their report, in their terms and credited; the atlas has not repeated their runs.
statement.reasons_heading: Why this file needs a careful reader
statement.checks_none: No reader has filed a check of this statement yet.
statement.replays_none: No independent Comparator replay has been shared yet.
statement.og_alt: Statement comparison for {label}: a candidate paper statement beside the Lean statement, with its scope and review status.
statement.holes_intro: Comparator checks only the name and type of each definition listed here. The body a proof is checked against is the definition in OpenAI’s solution library, so a reader must read it there as well as in this file.
statement.hole_item: Comparator checks the name and type of `{name}`; its definition is in OpenAI’s library at {link}.
statement.hole_item_nolink: Comparator checks the name and type of `{name}`; its definition is in OpenAI’s library, in the modules that `{module}` imports.
statement.card_holes_one: Comparator checks only the name and type of `{name}`; its body comes from the solution.
statement.card_holes_many: Comparator checks only the name and type of {n} definitions, among them `{name}`; their bodies come from the solution.
statement.coverage_heading: Scope according to OpenAI’s note (draft reading by an AI agent, unreviewed)
statement.coverage_source: OpenAI’s Lean note for this result
statement.coverage_stale: The draft scope reading was made for a different version of the release, so it is not shown.

coverage_classes.headline: States the paper’s headline theorem
coverage_classes.headline-part: States part of the headline theorem

statement.coverage_provenance: An AI agent classified OpenAI’s note; no person has reviewed the classification yet.
statement.comparator_box_heading: What an accepted Comparator run would establish
statement.comparator_box_does: If Comparator is run under this configuration and accepts, the solution proves the configured theorem using only the allowed axioms, and the Lean kernel accepts every step.
statement.comparator_box_holes: This configuration lists {n} definition holes: {names}. Comparator compares these by name and type only; their bodies come from the solution.
statement.comparator_box_noholes: This configuration lists no definition holes, so every definition the statement uses is compared as it is written in this file.
statement.comparator_box_not: An accepted run leaves three questions to a reader: whether this file says what the paper says, whether the paper's other claims are correct, and whether the result is new. Those need a signed statement check, the paper itself and the literature.

explain.title: Explain a result
explain.lede: Contribute an explanation for mathematicians outside a result’s area. {open} of {families} families have no explanation recorded in the atlas yet.
explain.how: Choose a family, read its statement and sources, then propose an explanation. The contributing guide sets out what to include and how the work is reviewed.
explain.queue_heading: Where a careful reading is most useful
explain.queue_intro: The first {n} of the {flagged} challenge files with a specific reason for a careful reading, each with its reasons.
explain.queue_not_verdict: The order allocates reading time and says nothing about whether any statement or proof is correct.

statements.title: Lean statements
statements.lede: The release’s {lean} Comparator challenge files. Each states the theorems its configuration names; OpenAI’s Lean catalogue (lean/formalization.yaml) lists {main} of them as main results. Sort by any column.
statements.filter: Filter by name, result or discipline

numbers.title: Numbers
numbers.lede: Counts from the release at commit {commit_short}, with what each counts and how.
numbers.upstream_intro: OpenAI’s reported figures and the atlas’s related counts, with the measure and source for each.
numbers.upstream_formalised_atlas: The atlas counts {n} current manuscripts listed as accompanying papers in family notes that link a Comparator statement, whatever part of the paper that statement covers. OpenAI’s figure counts formalised headline results.
numbers.upstream_catalogue_atlas: The atlas counts {manuscripts} current manuscripts in {families} families.
numbers.upstream_problems_atlas: The atlas does not count problems posed; the release does not list them.
numbers.scope_heading: Scope in OpenAI’s notes: the draft reading
numbers.scope_intro: An AI agent read OpenAI’s note for every Comparator challenge file and classified what each states. No person has reviewed these classifications yet. Unclear stays a class of its own.
numbers.scope_stale: The draft scope reading was made for a different version of the release, so its counts are not shown.
numbers.scope_families_no_full_headline: {n} families with linked statements, none classified as stating the paper’s headline theorem
numbers.scope_families_partial_headline_only: {n} families where a statement is classified as stating part of the headline theorem and none the whole of it
numbers.scope_families_with_lean_but_no_headline: {n} families where no statement is classified as stating the headline theorem or a part of it
numbers.scope_families_mixed_classes: {n} families whose statements fall in different classes

claims.heading: OpenAI’s Lean library: a source index
claims.intro: A textual scan of the Lean library at the pinned commit. Nothing is built, so a declaration listed here exists in the source; the scan records nothing about whether it was checked.
claims.projects_with_model_file: Distinct projects with a Model.lean file
claims.model_statement_projects_linked_to_a_fam: Projects with such definitions that are linked to a family
claims.direct: Of the {total} names containing ‘manuscript’, {n} occur directly in Comparator configurations’ theorem lists. A configured proof can use many other theorems, so this is a match of names only.

numbers.envs_intro: Counts of theorem-like environments extracted from the current manuscripts’ TeX sources, by kind. The extraction could not parse the sources of {unparsed} manuscripts.
numbers.withdrawn_intro: The release withdrew {n} manuscripts. Their notices are quoted in full.
numbers.changelog_source: Quoted from the release’s history file

families.label: families of related papers
families.definition: The numbered families of the release, each with one or more manuscripts. Some numbers in the sequence are unused.
families.how: Counted from the release’s overview.tex, which lists every family under its discipline, cross-checked against CONTENTS.md.

disciplines.label: disciplines
disciplines.definition: The subject headings under which the release’s overview groups its families.
disciplines.how: Counted from the section headings of overview.tex.

manuscripts_current.label: current manuscripts
manuscripts_current.definition: Manuscripts listed under a family in the release’s overview or contents list, in their current edition.
manuscripts_current.how: Every folder under preprints/ named by a family, excluding withdrawn manuscripts and earlier editions that a newer README replaces.

manuscripts_withdrawn.label: withdrawn manuscripts
manuscripts_withdrawn.definition: Manuscripts whose README carries a withdrawal notice.
manuscripts_withdrawn.how: Counted from the withdrawal notices in each preprint’s README.

manuscripts_previous_editions.label: earlier editions
manuscripts_previous_editions.definition: Manuscript folders that a newer edition lists as its previous version.
manuscripts_previous_editions.how: Counted from the previous-version links in each current README.

statements_lean.label: Comparator challenge files
statements_lean.definition: Lean files in lean/ComparatorChallenges/, each with a configuration naming the theorems or definitions Comparator compares against a solution. One file can hold several target theorems.

statements_lean_main_results.label: Comparator challenge files OpenAI lists as main results
statements_lean_main_results.definition: Comparator challenge files that OpenAI’s lean/formalization.yaml names in its main-results list. The release’s Lean notes link the other challenge files; formalization.yaml leaves them out.
statements_lean_main_results.how: Challenge files named by a main-result entry in lean/formalization.yaml.

main_result_declarations.label: main-result declarations
main_result_declarations.definition: Entries in the main-results list of the release’s formalisation record; one challenge file can carry several.
main_result_declarations.how: Counted from the main-results list in lean/formalization.yaml.

families_with_lean.label: families with a linked Comparator statement
families_with_lean.definition: Families whose Lean notes (lean/docs/NNN.md) link at least one Comparator challenge file.
families_with_lean.how: Counted from the statement rows of each family’s Lean notes.

manuscripts_with_lean.label: manuscripts with an accompanying Comparator statement
manuscripts_with_lean.definition: Current manuscripts listed as accompanying papers in a family’s Lean notes that link at least one Comparator statement, whatever part of the paper that statement covers.
manuscripts_with_lean.how: Current manuscripts named as accompanying papers in a family’s Lean notes, where those notes link at least one challenge file.

lean_statements_pure_mathlib.label: challenge files that import only Mathlib and add no local vocabulary
lean_statements_pure_mathlib.definition: Comparator challenge files whose imports are all Mathlib and in which no local vocabulary declaration is detected.
lean_statements_pure_mathlib.how: Challenge files whose imports are all Mathlib and which declare no definition, structure, instance, notation or axiom of their own.

lean_statements_no_local_vocabulary.label: challenge files with no local vocabulary
lean_statements_no_local_vocabulary.definition: Comparator challenge files in which no local vocabulary declaration is detected, whatever they import.
lean_statements_no_local_vocabulary.how: Challenge files with a local vocabulary count of zero.

lean_statements_with_custom_vocabulary.label: challenge files with local vocabulary
lean_statements_with_custom_vocabulary.definition: Comparator challenge files with at least one local vocabulary declaration: a definition, structure, instance, notation or axiom.
lean_statements_with_custom_vocabulary.how: Challenge files with a local vocabulary count of one or more.

lean_statements_importing_non_mathlib.label: challenge files importing from outside Mathlib
lean_statements_importing_non_mathlib.definition: Comparator challenge files with an import outside Mathlib.
lean_statements_importing_non_mathlib.how: Read from the import lines of each challenge file.

lean_statements_declaring_axioms.label: challenge files declaring an axiom
lean_statements_declaring_axioms.definition: Comparator challenge files with an axiom declaration of their own.
lean_statements_declaring_axioms.how: Read from the declarations of each challenge file.

lean_definition_holes.label: definition holes across all configurations
lean_definition_holes.definition: Definitions a configuration names for comparison by name and type only; their bodies come from the solution. These configurations have them:
lean_definition_holes.how: Counted from the definition_names list of each challenge configuration.

lean_vocabulary_total.label: local vocabulary declarations across all challenge files
lean_vocabulary_total.definition: Local vocabulary declarations: definitions, abbreviations, structures, classes, inductive types, instances, notation, macros and axioms detected in a challenge file. Theorem and lemma declarations are excluded. The count describes the file; it measures neither difficulty nor correctness.
lean_vocabulary_total.how: The local vocabulary counts of all challenge files, added up. A definition repeated in two files counts twice.

lean_vocabulary_median.label: median local vocabulary declarations per challenge file
lean_vocabulary_median.definition: Local vocabulary declarations: definitions, abbreviations, structures, classes, inductive types, instances, notation, macros and axioms detected in a challenge file. Theorem and lemma declarations are excluded.
lean_vocabulary_median.how: The median of the local vocabulary counts across all challenge files.

lean_vocabulary_max.label: largest local vocabulary count in one challenge file
lean_vocabulary_max.definition: Local vocabulary declarations: definitions, abbreviations, structures, classes, inductive types, instances, notation, macros and axioms detected in a challenge file. Theorem and lemma declarations are excluded. The file with the largest count is
lean_vocabulary_max.how: The largest local vocabulary count of any challenge file.

internal_citation_edges.label: citation links between manuscripts in the collection
internal_citation_edges.definition: Bibliography entries in a manuscript’s TeX sources that point to another manuscript in the collection, counted once per citing and cited manuscript. A citation records that one paper cites another.
internal_citation_edges.how: Read from each manuscript’s bibliography: entries linking to an openai/math preprint or keyed OAI:, once per pair.

manuscripts_citing_collection.label: manuscripts that cite another in the collection
manuscripts_citing_collection.definition: Current manuscripts with at least one citation to another manuscript in the collection.
manuscripts_citing_collection.how: Current manuscripts with one or more internal citations.

manuscripts_citing_unformalised_collecti.label: manuscripts citing a manuscript with no accompanying Comparator statement
manuscripts_citing_unformalised_collecti.definition: Current manuscripts that cite at least one manuscript in the collection that is not listed as an accompanying paper in family notes linking a Comparator statement.
manuscripts_citing_unformalised_collecti.how: Current manuscripts with an internal citation to a manuscript that no family’s Lean notes list as an accompanying paper.

external_works_cited.label: automatically grouped references outside the release
external_works_cited.definition: References outside the collection, grouped automatically by DOI, then arXiv identifier, then normalised title. Automatic grouping can merge two works or split one, so this approximates the number of distinct works.
external_works_cited.how: Every bibliography entry cited in a current manuscript’s text that points outside the collection, grouped across manuscripts by DOI, then arXiv identifier, then normalised title.

external_citations.label: resolved external reference keys (each manuscript and key counted once)
external_citations.definition: Resolved bibliography keys in the current manuscripts’ TeX sources that point outside the collection, each manuscript and key counted once.
external_citations.how: Counted from each manuscript’s cited bibliography entries.

recon.heading: How much of the release has Lean: the published counts
recon.intro: Several different counts of the release’s Lean coverage are in circulation. Each measures a different thing.
recon.families_with_lean_in_scope_notes: Families whose Lean notes (lean/docs) link at least one Comparator statement
recon.families_with_a_paper_in_formalization_y: Families with a paper in the sources list of OpenAI’s lean/formalization.yaml
recon.tier_list_families_with_lean: Families the OpenAI Math Tier List counts as having a Lean formalisation
recon.tier_list_lean_formalisations_total: Lean formalisations the Tier List counts in total (the figure some press reports quote as papers)
recon.mathvet_families_full: Families whose challenges state the headline in full, in MathVet’s reading
recon.mathvet_families_partial: Families where only a special case is stated, in MathVet’s reading
recon.mathvet_families_weaker_or_supporting: Families with only a weaker statement or supporting results, in MathVet’s reading
recon.cert_machine_families_matching: Families whose challenges match OpenAI’s headline, in Carlos Toledo’s cert-machine reading
recon.cert_machine_families_narrower_declared: Families stated more narrowly with OpenAI’s note saying so, in cert-machine’s reading
recon.cert_machine_families_narrower_undeclare: Families stated more narrowly where OpenAI’s note does not say so or the missing paper is unlinked, in cert-machine’s reading
recon.cert_machine_families_different_or_suppo: Families whose challenges state a different theorem or only supporting results, in cert-machine’s reading
recon.mathvet_challenges_accepted: Challenge files MathVet’s own Comparator runs accepted
recon.cert_machine_challenges_accepted: Challenge files cert-machine’s re-run accepted with both Lean’s kernel and nanoda
recon.note: The Tier List’s families with Lean are all among the families with a paper in OpenAI’s sources list, which the 7 October update extended. OpenAI’s Lean notes link Comparator statements for more families than its sources list names.

references_outside.title: References outside the release
references_outside.lede: The manuscripts in the release cite {works} automatically grouped references outside the collection, through {citations} resolved reference keys. These are the {n} references the most manuscripts cite, with every manuscript that cites each one.
references_outside.credit: The list records the works cited by the manuscripts and links the manuscripts that cite them.
references_outside.how: References are grouped automatically by DOI, then arXiv identifier, then normalised title, which can merge two works or split one. Each manuscript counts once per reference.

citations_within.title: Citations within the release
citations_within.lede: {edges} citation links run between manuscripts inside the collection, read from their bibliographies. These are the {n} manuscripts that the most other current manuscripts cite.
citations_within.cited_by: Cited by {n} manuscripts in the collection
citations_within.how: A citation counts when a manuscript’s bibliography points to another manuscript in the collection, once per citing and cited manuscript. A citation records that one paper cites another; how the cited result is used has not been examined here.

contribute.title: Contribute
contribute.lede: Contribute an explanation, a statement review, a source attribution, a replay record or a correction. Contributions are credited on the pages they change.
contribute.claim: Offer to write an explanation of one result.
contribute.check: Check a Lean statement against its paper and file what you found.
contribute.problem: Suggest a change or ask a precise question about one page, number or statement.
contribute.credit: Suggest an attribution for an idea, argument or earlier result.
contribute.replay: Share an independent Comparator replay of a statement.
contribute.guide: The contributing guide explains each in full.

about.title: About the atlas
about.what: The OpenAI Math Atlas is an independent guide to OpenAI’s mathematics release of {release_date}. It groups the manuscripts into {families} families of related papers, links the Lean statements accompanying {families_with_lean} families, and records citations and reader contributions.
about.how: Scripts read the release at commit {commit_short} and extract catalogue entries, available manuscript sources, bibliographies, Comparator files and scope notes. The generated pages link back to the source files. Catalogue counts come from the release; contribution status comes from the atlas’s own records.
about.independence: The atlas is an independent project. It is not affiliated with or endorsed by OpenAI. It describes what is in the release and what has been checked, and quotes OpenAI’s own words where it describes the results.
about.licence: The release is published by OpenAI under the Apache License 2.0. The atlas typesets selected descriptions, abstracts, statements and notes from the pinned release and links to their source files.
about.cite: Cite a page by its address and the pinned commit it describes.
about.author: {author} builds and maintains the atlas. His own work on Erdős problems, with its Lean proofs, is at Plectis.
about.made: Will Cook built the atlas with AI coding agents (Anthropic’s Claude) under his direction. The repository contains the scripts used to extract and count material from the pinned release. AI-made classifications, such as the scope of each Lean statement, are labelled as drafts and await human review. Named statement reviews and replay receipts are recorded separately.
about.not: The atlas records source material, review reports and replay receipts. It does not provide peer review or endorse the release’s results. Each page states which checks are recorded.

about.disclosed_intro: OpenAI’s README records the following about how the release was produced:

about.disclosed_not: The README reports average compute and the approximate number of problems posed. Prompts, per-result compute and the full list of attempted problems are absent from it.

community.title: Everyone working on this release
community.lede: {efforts} public efforts by {people} people have indexed, checked, replayed, explained or built on OpenAI’s release. {findings} of their findings attach to specific results, and each appears on that result’s page with its author’s name.
community.lede_empty: Public work by other people on this release is being gathered here, each piece credited and linked.
community.credit: The atlas exists alongside this work and draws on it. Findings are cited with their authors and links; code and text are reused only where the author’s licence allows it, and otherwise linked.
community.how: Each entry is a public project, paper, post or organisation, described in the atlas’s words with a link to the original. Listing someone’s work does not mean they endorse the atlas.

sources.title: Sources
sources.lede: Everything on the atlas comes from {sources} sources: OpenAI’s repository, the atlas’s own checks, and public work by {people} other people, with {findings} of their findings attached to specific results.
sources.credit: Other people’s data and findings are folded into the atlas’s own rows and credited at every point of use. Code, data files and prose are copied only where the author’s licence allows; otherwise the atlas cites the finding and links the original.
sources.openai_uses: The catalogue, the {manuscripts} current manuscripts in {families} families with their TeX sources and bibliographies, the {lean} Comparator challenge files and the Lean library, OpenAI’s Lean notes and its history file.
sources.atlas_uses: The atlas’s own extraction and checks: each paper’s extracted statements beside its Lean statement, a draft reading of what each Lean statement states, an index of the Lean library’s source, the citation records, references outside the release, and the reconciliation of published counts. The method follows Will Cook’s claim-faithful publication system for his Erdős problem corpus.
sources.ingested_heading: Data folded in from other people’s work
sources.ingested_intro: Each of these sources adds values to the atlas’s rows. Every value shows its source where it appears.
sources.efforts_heading: Findings and work cited from other people
sources.efforts_intro: Replays, error reports, follow-up results, explanations and commentary, each attached to the results it concerns and credited there.
